title_ar: الشيخ الددو : رفض الشعوب لصفقة القرن يبطلها
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew: The Peoples’ Rejection of the Deal of the Century Renders It Void
body_ar:
اسطنبول - صهيب قلالوة / الأناضول

اعتبر الموريتاني محمد الحسن ولد الددو، عضو الاتحاد العالمي لعلماء المسلمين، الاثنين، أن الرفض الشعبي لما يسمى بـ"صفقة القرن"، هو ما يحكم ببطلانها.

جاء ذلك في تصريح أدلى به ولد الددو للأناضول، على هامش مؤتمر صحفي عقد بمدينة إسطنبول، بمشاركة أكثر من 25 اتحادا وهيئة علمائية، في مقدمتهم، الاتحاد العالمي لعلماء المسلمين.

وقال ولد الددو إن "الناس (الشعوب) والفلسطينين والمسلمين والأمة الإسلامية، لن يقبلوا التنازل عن المسجد الأقصى ولا التطبيع" مع إسرائيل.

وشدد على أن "أرض فلسطين وقف إسلامي (...) والسعي لبيع المسجد الأقصى وما حوله من الأرض المباركة، لا يمكن أن يقره عقل أو منطق، ونؤمن أن ذلك لن يتحقق، وندعوا الجميع إلى استنكار هذه الورشة وما يترتب عليها".

وفي كلمته بالمؤتمر، أكد ولد الددو أن "صفقة القرن ليست صفقة في حقيقتها، وإنما هي انتزاع لبعض أموال المسلمين مقابل تلك الأرض، والحكم الشرعي واضح وهو أن هذه الورشة حرام شرعاً".

ولفت إلى أن "ورشة المنامة تستبطن الخنوع والذلة والمهانة، ولا بد من إظهار الاحتجاج على هذه الورشة، التي تنم عن التطبيع الممنوع والمحرم مع الكيان الإسرائيلي".

ورأى أن "الذين فكروا بصفقة القرن لن يستطيعوا، من خلالها، اتخاذ خطوات عملية، مع أنهم يظنون أنهم إذا جمعوا 50 مليار دولار من ورشة المنامة، فسيحققون نجاحا في ذلك".

والأحد، كشف جاريد كوشنر، صهر الرئيس الأمريكي دونالد ترامب، ومستشاره، عن أول جزء من خطة الولايات المتحدة من أجل السلام في الشرق الأوسط.

ويركز هذا الجزء على الجانب الاقتصادي؛ إذ تعتزم الإدارة الأمريكية استثمار حوالي 50 مليار دولار في المنطقة، نصف القيمة ستذهب للضفة الغربية وغزة، فيما يساهم النصف الآخر في دعم اقتصادات الأردن ولبنان ومصر، وفق كوشنر.

وينعقد "مؤتمر البحرين" بالمنامة، الثلاثاء والأربعاء المُقبليْن، تحت عنوان "ورشة الازدهار من أجل السلام"، وذلك في أول إجراء عملي لخطة السلام الأمريكية في الشرق الأوسط، المعروفة إعلاميا بـ"صفقة القرن".

وأعلنت السلطة والفصائل الفلسطينية عن رفضها للمؤتمر، ودعت إلى مقاطعته.

و"صفقة القرن"، خطة سلام أعدتها إدارة الرئيس الأمريكي دونالد ترامب، ويتردد أنها تقوم على إجبار الفلسطينيين على تقديم تنازلات مجحفة لمصلحة إسرائيل، بما فيها وضع مدينة القدس الشرقية المحتلة، وحق عودة اللاجئين. وقال ولد الددو إن "الناس (الشعوب) والفلسطينين والمسلمين والأمة الإسلامية، لن يقبلوا التنازل عن المسجد الأقصى ولا التطبيع" مع إسرائيل.

body_en:
Istanbul — Suhayb Qalalwa / Anadolu

The Mauritanian Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, member of the International Union of Muslim Scholars, held on Monday that the popular rejection of what is called the "Deal of the Century" is what rules it void.

This came in a statement made by Ould al-Dedew to Anadolu on the margins of a press conference held in the city of Istanbul with the participation of more than 25 unions and scholarly bodies, foremost among them the International Union of Muslim Scholars.

Ould al-Dedew said that "the people (the peoples), the Palestinians, the Muslims and the Muslim Ummah will not accept the surrender of the Aqsa Mosque, nor normalisation" with Israel.

He stressed that "the land of Palestine is an Islamic endowment (waqf) (…) and the attempt to sell the Aqsa Mosque and the blessed land around it is something no mind and no logic can accept. We believe that this will not come about, and we call on everyone to denounce this workshop and what follows from it."

In his address to the conference, Ould al-Dedew affirmed that "the Deal of the Century is not in truth a deal; it is rather the extraction of some of the Muslims' money in exchange for that land, and the ruling in Sharia is clear, namely that this workshop is forbidden (ḥarām) in law."

He noted that "the Manama workshop has within it submissiveness, abasement and humiliation. Protest against this workshop must be shown, for it bespeaks the normalisation with the Israeli entity that is prohibited and forbidden."

He held that "those who conceived the Deal of the Century will not be able, through it, to take practical steps, even though they suppose that if they gather 50 billion dollars from the Manama workshop they will achieve success in that."

On Sunday, Jared Kushner, son-in-law and adviser of the American president Donald Trump, unveiled the first part of the United States plan for peace in the Middle East.

This part concentrates on the economic side: the American administration intends to invest about 50 billion dollars in the region, half of the sum to go to the West Bank and Gaza, while the other half contributes to supporting the economies of Jordan, Lebanon and Egypt, according to Kushner.

The "Bahrain conference" convenes in Manama next Tuesday and Wednesday under the title "Peace to Prosperity Workshop", as the first practical step of the American peace plan for the Middle East, known in the media as the "Deal of the Century".

The Palestinian Authority and the Palestinian factions announced their rejection of the conference and called for it to be boycotted.

The "Deal of the Century" is a peace plan drawn up by the administration of the American president Donald Trump. It is reported to rest on compelling the Palestinians to make inequitable concessions in Israel's favour, including on the status of the occupied city of East Jerusalem and the right of return of the refugees.

[At this point the source record repeats itself. The whole passage from "Ould al-Dedew said that 'the people (the peoples)…'" down to "…and the right of return of the refugees." is served a second time, verbatim and without a paragraph break after the first occurrence. The repetition is preserved in body_ar and recorded as a source defect in the flags below; it is not reproduced a second time here, and nothing in it has been omitted from this translation.]

flags.arabic: وقال ولد الددو إن "الناس (الشعوب) ... وحق عودة اللاجئين. وقال ولد الددو إن "الناس (الشعوب) ...
flags.context: the body of the record, which serves the same block of text twice
options: treat the second occurrence as a CMS duplication and display the text once, as recommended here
display the record exactly as served, repetition included
withhold the record until the Sheikh's office confirms which text is intended
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT — INTERNAL DUPLICATION. The article body contains the whole passage from 'Ould al-Dedew said…' to '…the right of return of the refugees' twice over. The two copies are identical character for character, and the second begins immediately after the first with only a space, not a paragraph break, which is the signature of a paste error at entry rather than two distinct versions. The DOM was checked: #content holds a single article paragraph, so the repetition is in the stored record, not an artefact of extraction. body_ar preserves it in full. Flagged, not deduplicated unilaterally (style guide section 11).

flags.arabic: والحكم الشرعي واضح وهو أن هذه الورشة حرام شرعاً ... التطبيع الممنوع والمحرم مع الكيان الإسرائيلي
flags.context: the Sheikh's reported ruling on the Manama workshop and on normalisation
options: hold the record from publication pending legal advice in each jurisdiction
publish the report as translated, with a contextual note identifying the June 2019 Manama workshop
publish with the ruling carried only in the Arabic pane
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW. This is one of the few records in the slice in which a ruling is actually stated, and it is a ruling of ḥarām on participation in a named international economic conference and on normalisation with Israel. In several Western jurisdictions, advocacy of boycotts of Israel is restricted by statute or by public-procurement rules — notably in a number of US states and, in a different form, in Germany and France — and an English page carrying a religious ruling to that effect raises questions that are legal and reputational, not editorial. The translation is faithful: حرام شرعاً is 'forbidden (ḥarām) in law' by the fixed mapping, not 'discouraged'; الممنوع والمحرم is 'prohibited and forbidden', the doublet the Arabic uses; الكيان الإسرائيلي is rendered literally as 'the Israeli entity' rather than normalised to 'Israel', because the choice of phrase is the speaker's. The publication decision belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office, with legal advice.

flags.context: أن الرفض الشعبي لما يسمى بـ"صفقة القرن"، هو ما يحكم ببطلانها
options: rules it void (the technical sense: the deal is legally without effect)
flags.note: بطلان is the glossary's bāṭil, 'void' — a judgement about validity and legal effect, not about sin — and the English keeps that. Note the register: the subject of the verb is popular rejection, not a court, so 'rules' is doing metaphorical work in both languages. The headline is the news agency's summary, not a quotation from the Sheikh.

translator_notes: A news dispatch from the Anadolu Agency, republished on the Sheikh's site with the agency's byline intact. The framing sentences (the Kushner announcement, the description of the Bahrain conference, the description of the Deal of the Century) are the agency's, not the Sheikh's, and the English keeps that distinction visible — style guide section 1 on not collapsing a reported position into the speaker's own.
ورشة is the conference's own designation, 'workshop' (from its title, 'Peace to Prosperity Workshop'); it is not a loose word for a meeting and has been kept.
وقف is rendered 'endowment (waqf)' per the glossary, with the Arabic bracketed on first occurrence.
Source defects preserved in body_ar: اسطنبول in the dateline without hamzah while the body has إسطنبول with it; الفلسطينين for الفلسطينيين; وندعوا for وندعو.
The five rulings mapping of style guide section 3 is in play here and has been applied: حرام is 'forbidden'.

The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload/publication stamp, not the date on which the Sheikh gave the answer. Records across this slice carry timestamps clustered minutes apart on the same day (e.g. 1038/1039/1040 at 08:13/08:14/08:14 on 8 August 2019; 1077/1078/1079 at 09:50/09:52/09:53 on 22 July 2020), which is the signature of a batch upload. date_is_cms_upload is therefore set true throughout.
